subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a modular internal installer layout while preserving the public single-file `install.sh` contract?
rationale: This is not a broken behavior report; it changes the architecture of a public setup surface whose docs, tests, website sync, and release validation currently assume one shell script.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded split
options.body: Approve a design where modules are source-only or bundled into one served script, with website sync and installer smoke proof updated in the same plan.

options.title: Keep focused refactors only
options.body: Leave the issue as backlog guidance and extract/delete sections only when tied to concrete installer bugs or validation improvements.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decide the public shell installer should remain monolithic to avoid helper-loading and packaging risk.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a guarded split
recommendation.body: Approve a design where modules are source-only or bundled into one served script, with website sync and installer smoke proof updated in the same plan.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the clearest current owner for the single-file installer tests and public website sync path that define the compatibility boundary.
